text: Why did IPv6 remove router fragmentation entirely?
choices: Because it is stateful and expensive at the destination, multiplies effective loss, hides transport headers from firewalls, and interacts badly with NAT and ECMP
Because IPv6 packets are always small
explanation: Only the source may fragment; routers send ICMP Packet Too Big instead. This makes Path MTU Discovery mandatory rather than optional, which is why blocking ICMPv6 breaks IPv6 outright rather than merely degrading it.
